q: 1. Pick up the constituent of good brick earth whose excess causes the raw bricks shrink and warp during drying and burning, from the following
explain: Excess lime forms lumps that absorb moisture and expand on burning, causing bricks to crack and warp.

q: 2. Porcelain is used as
explain: Porcelain's smooth, non-porous, vitrified surface makes it the standard material for sanitary fittings.

q: 3. The indentation provided in a face of the brick is called
explain: The frog is the depression pressed into a brick's face, which helps key the brick to the mortar.

q: 4. The red color obtained by the bricks is due to the presence of
explain: Iron oxide in the clay oxidizes during burning, giving bricks their characteristic red color.

q: 5. Ceramic material is manufactured from
options: natural clays and minerals admixture at high temperature
explain: Ceramics are inorganic, non-metallic materials processed by shaping and then firing at high temperatures (vitrification).

q: 6. The impurity not desirable in the soil used for brick formation is
explain: Alkalis cause efflorescence (white staining), while Kankar (lime nodules) can cause bricks to split upon hydration.

q: 7. The standard size of a brick as per Nepal Standard (NS) is
explain: The Nepal Standard (NS) specifies the brick size as 230mm x 115mm x 57mm.

q: 8. The main function of alumina in brick earth is
explain: Alumina absorbs water and renders the clay plastic, which is essential for the molding of the brick.

q: 9. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make brick is called
explain: Tempering is the process of adding water to the brick earth and kneading it to achieve a uniform, plastic mass.

q: 10. The ingredient of the brick earth which enables the brick to retain shape is
explain: Alumina imparts plasticity to clay, allowing the brick to be molded and retain its shape.

q: 11. The over ground continuous kiln is called
explain: A tunnel kiln is built above ground and operates continuously as bricks move through it on trolleys.

q: 12. If iron oxide present in brick earth is more than the requirement then colour of the brick after burning will be
explain: Excess iron oxide oxidizes further during burning, deepening the red color of the fired brick.

q: 13. Bull nose bricks are not used in
explain: Bullnose bricks have rounded edges and are used for corners or pillars, but they are not standard for arch construction.

q: 14. Fire bricks are used
explain: Refractory bricks have low thermal conductivity, helping to contain heat within a furnace and decrease outward heat flow.

q: 15. The bricks are properly soaked in water before use the following reason
options: to wash the kiln dust for better bondage with mortar
to avoid the chances of absorption of water from the mortar
to spread the mortar uniformly between them
explain: Soaking ensures the bricks don't suck water from the mortar (which weakens it) and removes dust for better adhesion.

q: 16. For manufacture of bricks normally the top soil is removed having a depth of .....
explain: The top 20cm of soil is usually stripped away (unsoiling) as it contains organic matter and impurities unsuitable for bricks.

q: 17. Tampering of soil for manufacture of bricks, is done by
explain: Kneading the soil (tempering) can be done manually by feet, using cattle, or mechanically in a pug mill.

q: 18. In case of clamp for burning of bricks, the bricks/ fuel are laid at a slope of...
explain: Clamps are constructed with a slight inward slope, usually around 15 degrees, to ensure stability as the fuel burns away.

q: 19. Refractory bricks are
explain: Refractory bricks are categorized into three types—acidic, basic, and neutral—based on their chemical resistance to slag.

q: 20. If rain water falls on hot bricks then the shape of the brick gets deformed, this defect is known as
explain: Chuffs is the defect caused when falling rain hits hot, newly burnt bricks, resulting in cracking and deformation.

q: 21. Dolomite bricks are
explain: Dolomite is a basic material; therefore, bricks made from it are classified as basic refractory bricks.

q: 22. Jhumb bricks
explain: Jhumb bricks (or Jhama bricks) are over-burnt bricks that have become vitrified and often distorted in shape.

q: 23. The reason for the popularity of bricks as construction material is that
options: they are cheap and available locally at all places
they are durable and possess fairly good strength and lighter than stones
they have very good insulating property against heat and sound
explain: Bricks are widely used due to their cost-effectiveness, durability, ease of handling, and natural insulation properties.

q: 24. The standard size of brick as per Indian standard is
explain: The standard modular brick size as per IS: 1077 is 19 cm x 9 cm x 9 cm.

q: 25. The soil used for the manufacture of bricks should preferably not contain the following material
explain: Alkalies cause efflorescence, while pebbles and kankar lead to cracking and weakness in the finished brick.

q: 26. Which of the following ingredients of brick earth enables the brick to retain its shape?
explain: Silica provides the structural bulk and rigidity that helps the brick retain its shape after molding and firing.

q: 27. Efflorescence is caused if
options: the alkaline salt is present in the bricks
the clay used for making bricks contain pyrite
the water used for pugging the clay contains gypsum
explain: Efflorescence can arise from multiple sources of soluble salts — alkalies in the clay, pyrite, or gypsum-contaminated water — all of which crystallize on the surface.

q: 28. The frog of a brick is normally made on its
explain: The frog is pressed into the top (frog) face of the brick during molding, which also helps key it to the mortar above.

q: 29. The maximum percentages of warping along the sides of tiles, is
explain: Quality control standards for tiles generally allow for a maximum of 2% warping along the edges.

q: 30. The internal size of mould used in brick preparation is
options: equal to the size of a fully burnt brick
smaller than the size of a fully burnt brick
greater than the size of a fully burnt brick
explain: The mould is made larger than the final brick size to account for shrinkage that occurs during drying and burning.

q: 31. If the water absorption of bricks is 5% of its weight, the brick may be
explain: A very low water absorption of 5% indicates a dense, high-quality brick, typical of heavy duty machine-made bricks.

q: 32. The colour of fire bricks is generally
explain: Fire bricks, made from fire clay low in iron oxide, typically fire to a yellowish-white color.

q: 33. Which of the following pairs gives a correct combination of the useful and harmful constituents respectively of a good brick earth?
explain: Silica is a useful (structural) constituent of brick earth, while alkalies are harmful, causing efflorescence.

q: 34. Number of brick required for one cubic meter of brick masonry is ( as per IS)
explain: As per this reference (IS), about 500 bricks are typically required per cubic meter of brick masonry.

q: 35. A queen closer is a
options: brick laid with its length parallel to the face or direction of wall
brick laid with its breadth parallel to the face or direction of wall
brick having the same length and depth as the other bricks but half the breadth
brick with half the width at one end and full width at the other
explain: A queen closer retains the full length and depth of a standard brick but has its breadth (width) halved.

q: 36. The slenderness ratio for masonry walls should not be more than
explain: For structural stability, the slenderness ratio of masonry walls is generally limited to a maximum of about 20.

q: 37. As compared to English bond, double flemish bond is
explain: Double Flemish bond requires more skilled labor and careful brick selection for its decorative pattern, making it costlier than English bond.

q: 38. Special material of construction capable of withstanding high temperature is:
explain: Refractory materials are specifically engineered to withstand very high temperatures without degrading.

q: 39. Hollow bricks are used for:
explain: The trapped air pockets in hollow bricks reduce heat transfer, providing thermal insulation.
